API Reference

This section provides a detailed reference for the public API of the naq library.

The API is organized into modules, each providing specific functionality.

Core Modules

  • queue Module: The primary interface for enqueuing and scheduling jobs. Includes the Queue class and helper functions like enqueue, enqueue_at, and schedule.

  • job Module: Defines the Job class, which represents a unit of work to be executed.

  • worker Module: Contains the Worker class, responsible for executing jobs from one or more queues.

  • scheduler Module: Contains the Scheduler class, responsible for enqueuing scheduled and recurring jobs.

  • connection Module: Provides utilities for managing NATS connections, including connection monitoring, metrics tracking, and connection pooling.

  • exceptions Module: Defines custom exceptions raised by naq.

  • utils Module: Provides utility functions and classes for common functionality used throughout the NAQ codebase, including validation, error handling, serialization, and more.

Services

  • services Module: Provides a comprehensive service layer with modular components for connection management, job processing, event logging, and more. Includes the ServiceManager for dependency injection, service lifecycle management, and performance monitoring.

  • kv_stores Module: Provides a robust, centralized service for managing NATS KeyValue stores with support for pooling, transactions, and TTL.

Service Layer Architecture

The service layer is the foundation of NAQ’s modular architecture, providing a clean separation of concerns and enabling flexible composition of functionality. Each service is designed to be:

  • Modular: Can be used independently or composed with other services
  • Configurable: Supports both centralized and service-specific configuration
  • Monitorable: Built-in performance tracking and health monitoring
  • Extensible: Easy to extend with custom functionality

Core Services

Service Description Key Features
ConnectionService Manages NATS connections and JetStream contexts Connection pooling, caching, automatic reconnection
ConfigService Provides centralized configuration management Environment variables, hierarchical settings, validation
JobService Handles job execution and lifecycle management Result storage, event logging, retry handling
KVStoreService Manages NATS KeyValue stores Transactions, TTL, history tracking
EventService Logs and retrieves system events Configurable retention, event types, filtering
StreamService Manages JetStream streams Stream creation, consumer management, message publishing
WorkerService Tracks worker status and job processing Heartbeat monitoring, job registration, lifecycle management
SchedulerService Handles job scheduling and triggering Cron expressions, one-time schedules, recurring jobs

ServiceManager

The ServiceManager is the central component that orchestrates all services:

from naq.services.base import ServiceManager

async def main():
    # Create and initialize service manager
    manager = ServiceManager()
    await manager.initialize_all()
    
    # Access services as needed
    connection_service = manager.get_service(ConnectionService)
    job_service = manager.get_service(JobService)
    
    # Use services...
    
    # Cleanup all services
    await manager.cleanup_all()

Service Configuration

Services can be configured through the centralized configuration system:

from naq.services.base import ServiceConfig
from naq.services.connection import ConnectionServiceConfig

# Create service-specific configuration
connection_config = ConnectionServiceConfig(
    servers=["nats://localhost:4222"],
    max_reconnect_attempts=10
)

# Apply to service
service_config = ServiceConfig(custom_settings=connection_config.as_dict())
connection_service = ConnectionService(config=service_config)
